config.title: CSS Modules

intro.title: CSS Modules
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that uses CSS Modules to style a button and a heading. You will learn how CSS Modules work by scoping CSS class names locally to a component, preventing style conflicts. The main technologies involved are Vue single-file components (.vue files) and the `module` attribute on `<style>` tags. By the end, you'll understand how to import and apply scoped CSS classes in your template using Vue's `$style` object.
intro.usecase: CSS Modules are essential in large-scale Vue applications where component reuse and style isolation prevent conflicts. In enterprise dashboards with multiple interactive panels like data charts, filters, and modals, each component needs encapsulated styles to avoid unintended overrides. E-commerce product pages with dynamic UI elements such as size selectors, color pickers, and recommendation carousels rely on CSS Modules to maintain consistent, conflict-free styling. This approach is also critical in design systems where reusable UI components must function predictably across different sections of an application without global CSS collisions.

objectives: Apply CSS Modules to scope styles locally within a Vue component
Configure a Vue project to support CSS Modules without build tool conflicts
Bind scoped CSS classes to template elements using dynamic class objects
Manipulate component appearance by toggling CSS Modules classes with reactive data
Integrate multiple CSS Modules class bindings on a single element for combined styling
Construct a Vue component that uses CSS Modules for encapsulated, maintainable styling

steps.title: Add inline styles to the heading
steps.instruction: In your template, add a style attribute to the heading element to set its color to 'darkblue' and font-size to '2rem'.
steps.hint: Use the style attribute directly on the heading element with CSS property-value pairs.

successCriteria: The heading element has a style attribute with color: darkblue and font-size: 2rem.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create a CSS module file and import it
steps.instruction: Create a CSS module file named 'styles.module.css' in the same directory as your Vue component,
steps.hint: Create a new file with the .module.css extension, then use the import statement in your Vue component to bring in the CSS module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a CSS module in a Vue component
import styles from './styles.module.css'
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS module file is created and imported into the Vue component, making the module's styles available for use.
successCriteria: A 'styles.module.css' file exists and is imported into the component using 'import styles from './styles.module.css''.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've both created the CSS module file and imported it correctly in your component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS module file wasn't properly created or imported. Remember to create 'styles.module.css' and import it using 'import styles from './styles.module.css''.

steps.title: Define a CSS class in the module file
steps.instruction: Open the styles.module.css file and add a CSS class named 'highlight' with a background color of lightyellow and padding of 10px.
steps.hint: In the CSS module file, define a class selector starting with a dot, followed by the class name and curly braces containing the CSS properties.

/* styles.module.css */
/* Add your CSS class definition here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS module file now contains a class definition that can be imported and used in the Vue component.
successCriteria: The styles.module.css file contains a '.highlight' class with background-color: lightyellow and padding: 10px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a CSS class, but it might be missing some required properties. Make sure it has both background-color: lightyellow and padding: 10px.

steps.title: Apply the CSS module class to the paragraph
steps.instruction: In your Vue component, bind the imported CSS module class to the paragraph element using the :class directive.
steps.hint: Use :class='$style.className' syntax to apply the CSS module class to the paragraph element.
steps.analogousExample: // Applying a CSS module class to an element
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph element will have the CSS module class bound to it using :class.
successCriteria: The paragraph element uses :class with $style.className syntax to apply the CSS module class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the :class directive with $style.className syntax to bind the CSS module class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element doesn't have the CSS module class applied correctly. Use :class='$style.className' to bind the class.

steps.title: Add a second CSS class to the module file
steps.instruction: Open the styles.module.css file and define a second CSS class named 'highlight' with a different style, such as a background color.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule in the module file with a class name and styling properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The module file now contains two CSS classes: 'paragraphStyle' and 'highlight'.
successCriteria: A CSS class named 'highlight' is defined in styles.module.css with at least one style property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a CSS class, but make sure it's named 'highlight' and has at least one style property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS class 'highlight' is not defined correctly in the module file.

steps.title: Apply multiple CSS module classes to an element
steps.instruction: In your component, add a new <div> element and apply both CSS module classes (paragraphStyle and your second class) to it using array syntax with $style.
steps.hint: Use the $style object to access both classes and combine them in an array for the class binding.
steps.analogousExample:
// Applying multiple CSS module classes
Content with two classes
steps.expectedOutcome: A new div element will appear with both CSS module classes applied, demonstrating how to combine multiple classes from a CSS module.
successCriteria: The new div element uses array syntax with $style to apply both CSS module classes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using array syntax with $style to apply both classes to the div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you added a new div element and used :class="[$style.paragraphStyle, $style.yourSecondClass]" to apply both CSS module classes.

steps.title: Add a button element to the template
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the template with the text content 'Click me'.
steps.hint: Use the <button> HTML tag and place it after the existing paragraph.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button to a Vue template
<button>Submit</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button with the text 'Click me' appears in the UI below the paragraph.
successCriteria: The template contains a <button>Click me</button> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a button element to the template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an element, but it might not be a button or have the correct text. Check that you used <button>Click me</button>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or incorrect. Add <button>Click me</button> to the template.

steps.title: Style the button using CSS Modules
steps.instruction: Add a CSS class named 'buttonStyle' to your module file and apply it to the button element in your template using $style.buttonStyle.
steps.hint: In the <style module> section, define a .buttonStyle class with some styling properties. Then in the template, add :class="$style.buttonStyle" to the button element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button element will have a CSS module class applied, demonstrating how to style interactive elements with CSS Modules.
successCriteria: A .buttonStyle class is defined in the <style module> section and applied to the button element using :class="$style.buttonStyle".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both the CSS class definition and the class application are complete. Check that you've defined .buttonStyle in the <style module> section and applied it to the button with :class="$style.buttonStyle".
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't styled with CSS Modules yet. Remember to define a .buttonStyle class in the <style module> section and apply it to the button element using :class="$style.buttonStyle".
